newsitem.title: USA: IBP says will maintain reduced beef output.
newsitem.headline: IBP says will maintain reduced beef output.

text.p: IBP Inc plans to continue operating its 12 beef plants at reduced capacity during November because of low supplies of finished cattle, the company said Tuesday.

"Reduced supplies of finished cattle together with a higher proportion of 'green' cattle coming to market have resulted in lower weights and yields as well as lower margins," the company said in a statement.
IBP spokesman Gary Mickelson told Reuters the company's beef plants would be operating 32 to 40 hours a week, compared with a normal 48-hour week.

Mickelson also said there were no new developments in a meatcutters strike at IBP's Joslin, Ill., beef plant. The plant has been shut down for the past week. Mickelson said IBP has shifted the plant's production to other plants.

No negotiations were scheduled this week. About 1,800 members of United Food and Commercial Workers Union local 1540 struck the plant on November 12 after rejecting the company's latest contract offer.
